algorithm: Map tenants to reusable child processes. Admission happens before startup. Parent uses a pipe with a deadline; timeout retires and kills the worker. Warm requests reuse a process, while cold mode retires after each request. Wasmtime uses fuel with no WASI/host imports. Reference: https://bytecodealliance.github.io/wasmtime-py/ .
architecture: Workload API → tenant admission → bounded scheduler → dedicated process pipe → validated handler → result. Optional WebAssembly module is a separate execution backend helper.
data_model: Request = tenant, registered function, validated JSON payload. Response = status and result/error. Metrics reconcile successful, limited, timed-out and failed requests.
description: A local trusted-handler execution platform with per-tenant process reuse, quotas, failure responses and enforced deadlines.
design: Separate user identity, quotas and worker state. Never eval user strings. An untrusted platform needs an audited runtime with OS resource limits and syscall isolation; that boundary is not represented by Python processes.
family_notes: Reuse one worker for repeat requests.
Create and retire a process for each cold request.
Reject requests beyond the tenant admission quota.
Terminate a worker whose sleep handler exceeds its deadline.
Return handler errors without losing request accounting.
Keep reusable workers separate for two tenants.
limitations: Default Python workers run trusted registered functions only; process separation is NOT an untrusted-code sandbox. No arbitrary snippets, Firecracker, containerd, cloud deployment or millisecond cold-start guarantee. Requests are sequential in workloads, and quotas are lifetime-per-experiment rather than rate windows. Wasmtime optional path is unexecuted because the dependency is unavailable.
operations: Close the scheduler to retire workers. Deploy only predefined trusted handlers by default. Optional Wasmtime requires installing wasmtime and separately reviewing runtime/module limits.
scope: Multiprocessing worker pool, predefined validated handlers, tenant-owned reuse, bounded process count, admission quotas, wall-clock deadlines with termination, and optional import-free Wasmtime add module with fuel and memory limits.
security: Do not submit or execute untrusted Python code. The registered handlers are fixed and validated. Process separation is operational isolation only; a hosted untrusted service requires an audited sandbox and OS limits.
title: Multi-Tenant Serverless FaaS Platform
